findings.summary: The producer cannot see the loop-replay share unless the replay sends the work back, so it cannot write the measured figure, and no test can assert it.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs:370-399: `loop_replay = self.loop_replay(ctx, &snapshot)?; let held = loop_replay.as_ref().filter(|l| l.run.held); … if let Some(replay) = held { problems.push(replay_problem(replay)); }`. The share reaches the producer only inside a held send-back. run/mod.rs:2262 and 2172-2179 print the replay line with `ctx.ui.line`, which is Athena's UI, not the producer's tools. System facts: the producer snapshot has no records/, so the producer cannot run the replay itself. When the share is 8% or less, step 8's 'Read the loop-replay line … write the measured figure' cannot be done. The criterion-7 test needle 'the loop-replay measured share where it differs from 3' cannot be written either. Fix: Restate the measurement path honestly. The doc comment, CHANGELOG and D164 carry 'expected 3% of newly refused readings, an estimate'. The measured share goes into the job's replay record at verification (replay_stage → run.record), where the verifier sees it. The producer writes a measured figure only when a held send-back reports one (replay_problem gives the percent and the limit). Remove the 'measured share where it differs' needle from defined_terms_refusal_is_declared_intended. In D164, say where the measured figure is recorded.
findings.location: Plan step 8; Risks item 1; Decision 5; Criterion 7 demonstration ('the loop-replay measured share where it differs from 3')

findings.summary: Two of the four words, 'tier' and 'layer', are common engineering words with plain meanings. 'Tier' is also an established Athena concept (priority tiers), so ordinary requests will be refused. The plan neither states this false-refusal class nor pins it.
findings.evidence: plan.rs:421, 497, 733-741, drain.rs:612, config.rs:59 and display.rs:584 all use 'tier' for priority tiers ('demoted one tier because their tier was full'). A request such as 'Demote an item one tier when its tier is full' or 'add a caching layer' would be refused until the reading adds a Term line. The brief fixes the list and accepts the extra refusals for ladder and rung only. Where the plan states what is not covered, it lists only quoted mentions, terms outside the list and Hermes. Fix: Keep the list, which the brief fixes. Add an explicit limit to the doc comment and D164: plain technical uses of 'tier' (priority tiers) and 'layer' (caching layer) are refused too, and this is part of the intended rate. Add one corpus case that pins the known false refusal (a priority-tier request refused by check_defined_terms), so a later narrowing is a visible change.
findings.location: Approach / Decision 5: term list ladder, rung, tier, layer

findings.summary: The generated-line skip matches the bare prefix 'introspection ', and 'cause:' or 'failure class:' at any line start. A hand-written request line that starts with these words is dropped whole, including any real use of a term.
findings.evidence: hestia.rs:487 builds exactly `Introspection {id} (job {job}); prevention it proposed: …`. The brief names the shape 'Introspection <id> ... prevention it proposed:'. The plan only checks that the trimmed lowercase line starts with `introspection `. Fix: Match the generated shape. Skip an Introspection line only when it holds '; prevention it proposed:' (or match the id and '(job ' pattern). Skip Cause:/Failure class: lines only in the case-sensitive form hestia writes. Add a unit case: 'Introspection of the ladder is needed.' is still a use.

findings.summary: The matcher misses some real uses, and the definition check does not normalise plurals.
findings.evidence: request_words (reading.rs:3520-3523) keeps `'` between letters inside a word, so "the ladder's rungs" yields the token "ladder's", which matches no term. A parenthesised span with a comma, such as '(the ladder, which ranks requirements)', is dropped as an example list. A request using 'layers' with a reading that writes 'Term layers:' is refused, because the plan matches term or term+s in the request but a definition is a bare `term <word>:`. Fix: Strip a trailing `'s` from tokens before comparing. Normalise a definition word by dropping a trailing 's' when the base form is in STRUCTURAL_TERMS. Treat a parenthesised span as a list only when it holds two or more commas or opens with an example word, and add unit cases for each shape.

findings.summary: The test that deletes the line from READING_SOURCE and asserts acceptance_check_names stops listing the check tests only the text extractor. It does not show the gate's behavior changing.
findings.evidence: The plan: 'removes the new line from READING_SOURCE and asserts acceptance_check_names no longer lists the check'. That holds for any string-filter extractor, whatever refusing_check does. The behavior evidence for criterion 4 is the corpus refusal case plus defined_terms_refusal_needs_the_step_line, which uses gate_refuser, as history_fixture_refusal_needs_the_step_line does at reading.rs:10552-10567. Fix: Drop the source-doctoring test, or label it an extractor test. Rest criterion 4 on the gate-level tests: gate_refuser(reading) == Some("check_defined_terms"), and the corpus case refused under that name. Say in the demonstration that removing the step! line makes these fail.
findings.location: Criterion 4 demonstration: the source-doctoring test in refusal_corpus.rs

findings.summary: Criterion 2 asks for a case built from this retry's own root-cause request. The plan rebuilds the request from the corpus template and does not say so.
findings.evidence: The request of 20261107-110049-k8c2 is not in the snapshot (records/ is absent). root_cause_request at refusal_corpus.rs:236 is 'Rebuilt from the shape of job 20261030-170757-gev8's request'. Case.source must say whether the text is verbatim or rebuilt (refusal_corpus.rs:59). Fix: Set source to 'job 20261107-110049-k8c2, rebuilt from the job brief; not the recorded request', and name the shapes it reproduces: the hestia.rs:466-489 line forms and the parenthesised list.

summary: The plan reads the request correctly. It names real code: refusing_check and its step! lines (reading.rs:3242-3254), request_words (3507), check_outcome_state's doc comment (3653-3679), replay_declaration (4964), CITED_REQUESTS, root_cause_request, base_reading and INPUT_FORMS (34 entries) in refusal_corpus.rs, and READING_RULES with its test in briefs.rs (2225, 4401). Its placement after check_environment_reach is right: the two pinned adjacencies (8374-8377, 8852-8856) both stay intact. I checked the recorded 7bf8 text against the planned quote rule: the single-quoted addendum title is stripped, and 'Use the ladder…' stays as a plain use. The 0wtc text holds none of the four words, and the apostrophe in "Sri's" does not open a quote. So the corpus cases and the replay would show criteria 1, 2, 3 and 5 with the real gate, not a double. One part of the design is wrong. Step 8, the first risk mitigation and criterion 7's demonstration all expect the producer to 'read the loop-replay line printed in the producer loop' and write the measured share into the docs. But loop_replay runs in Athena's run code (run/mod.rs:2250) and prints to Athena's UI (`ctx.ui.line`). The producer sees a share only through replay_problem, which is called only when the replay is held over the limit (producer.rs:371, 398-399). Below 8%, the producer can neither see the figure nor write it, and no test can assert it. The rest are minor: three soundness gaps in the matcher, a criterion-4 test that only checks the extractor, and the criterion-2 request being rebuilt from the template, not taken from a record. No athena.toml field, landing rule or external service is involved. The dependents list covers what I found by grepping for readers of refusing_check, READING_RULES, the check_outcome_state doc comment, CITED_REQUESTS and the decision log. The tier/rung/ladder uses in athena-cli tests are identifiers, not request text.
